beginner.headline: The Leonid Meteor Shower Starts This Weekend
beginner.brief: The Leonid meteor shower starts this weekend. Its meteors look like lines of light that move quickly across the sky. The shower lasts until 30 November. It will be strongest on the night of 17 November. You may see as many as 15 meteors in an hour. Experts say to find a safe, dark place away from street lights. You can see the meteors with just your eyes. Give your eyes about 20 to 30 minutes to get used to the dark. An open space gives you a wide view of the sky. You need clear skies to see the meteors.

intermediate.headline: Leonid Meteor Shower Expected to Peak on 17 November
intermediate.brief: The Leonid meteor shower is expected to be visible across the UK during November. The shower continues until 30 November and is expected to reach its peak on the night of 17 November. Viewers could spot as many as 10 to 15 meteors in an hour. As the comet Tempel-Tuttle travels around the Sun, it leaves behind a trail of dust particles. These particles enter the layer of air around Earth at speeds of up to 71 kilometres per second, producing streaks of light. Experts recommend finding a safe, dark place away from light pollution, which is unwanted light from sources such as street lights. You can see the meteors with the naked eye, so you do not need binoculars or a telescope. Allow about 20 to 30 minutes for your eyes to adjust to the dark so that you have a better chance of spotting the meteors. An open area gives you a wide view of the night sky. Although the forecast calls for dry weather much of the time, clouds may still block the view in many areas. Fog could also form in places where the sky stays clear for a while, making the meteors harder to see. Anyone who misses the meteors this weekend may have better viewing conditions near the peak in mid-November. Near the peak, the Moon will be below the horizon around midnight, so its light is less likely to spoil the view.

advanced.headline: Leonid Meteor Shower to Peak on 17 November
advanced.brief: The Leonid meteor shower is set to begin this weekend and continue through the end of November. The shower is expected to reach its peak on the night of 17 November. The report estimates that observers might see as many as 10 to 15 meteors per hour. The shower originates in dust that Comet 55P/Tempel-Tuttle leaves in its wake as it orbits the Sun. Those particles can enter Earth’s atmosphere at up to 71 kilometres per second, a speed the report says makes the Leonids the fastest meteors in the sky. The Leonids’ radiant, the point from which they appear to emerge, lies near the head of the constellation Leo. That part of the sky offers a point of reference, although the meteors can appear anywhere in the sky. Experts advise seeking a safe, dark site well removed from sources of light pollution such as street lighting. The meteors can be seen without optical aids such as binoculars or a telescope. Allowing 20 to 30 minutes for your eyes to acclimatise to the dark can improve your chances of seeing the meteors. Dry though the weather is expected to be much of the time, extensive cloud is forecast in many areas. For Friday and Saturday nights, the forecast favours southern and western parts of England and Wales, where clear skies look more likely. More of the UK is likely to see clear skies by Sunday night. Fog could still form where skies stay clear for some time, obscuring the view. The report anticipates favourable viewing conditions around the peak, when the Moon will be below the horizon around midnight and its reflected light is less likely to interfere.
